crossStackDependencies.reason: The later error-reporting and provider-attribution patches modify the extracted external-agent-migration crate introduced by this other_codex_rs commit.
The raw-response schema update expects the protocol-level cache-write token accounting added by the companion other_codex_rs commit.
The target lacks the preceding credential-source, managed Bedrock login, and managed logout sequence that this stack reshapes and tests.
The streaming handoff stack follows the core realtime delegation tagging change and also requires the earlier V3/Frameless substrate absent from the target.
The fork fix extends the persisted reviewer restoration helper introduced by the earlier resume-thread change, which is not present in the target.
All three patches extend the persisted WorldState/diff foundation introduced before the #408 window; the target lacks that foundation entirely.
The generic Audio/LocalAudio and tool-output InputAudio protocol stack must exist before forwarding, modality filtering, and history preservation can work.
The later MCP binding/resource-client lineage assumes a thread-owned runtime, so the preliminary refactor should be staged with the adapted final MCP catalog work.
Lineage resolution and cleanup safety rely on history_base/HistoryPosition and subagent history boundaries introduced by the inherited-prefix stack.
Lineage-aware list/read/model-context behavior expects paginated thread metadata, memory mode, and Git metadata to remain consistent in SQLite.
The metadata stack writes more state through SQLite and benefits from the centralized WAL/busy-timeout connection behavior already present in Every Code.

Upstream #34629 carries an optional proxy restricting-SID parameter introduced by #34613. Port the ACL and runner hardening independently, adapting that optional interface until the managed-ingress work is staged.
The network-policy callback contract should follow, not precede, an end-to-end modern sandboxed exec-server path and an Every Code-owned decision flow.

Gating tui::restore() behind #[cfg(unix)] (#34578) is only safe after the RestoreMode enum is removed (#34551, in the jif cleanup stack), because Every Code's RestoreMode::Full still references restore().
Within the agent-picker stack, #33922 (path-backed agents) is a direct follow-up to #33921 (liveness); both are not_applicable to Every Code's simpler picker and neither lands without the other.
Within the side-conversations stack, #34199 fixes liveness races introduced by the exclude_turns fork in #34198 and must land after it.
Within the exec-output stack, bounded live output (#34359) builds on the preview/transcript iterator APIs introduced in #34357.

Both are markdown/transcript allocation refactors from the same upstream lineage; if adopted they should be sequenced together against Every Code's divergent markdown_stream pipeline, though neither strictly requires the other.
Backend, cloud-task, daemon, and LM Studio migrations require the shared route-aware client and proxy-policy foundation.
Auth and refresh requests must obtain their resolved client route from the shared HTTP routing layer.
Login and cloud-auth callers depend on the shared builder and request execution conventions established by the integration migrations.

reviewerNotes.note: The Every Code prealignment tree was consulted for product-sensitive paths: external import/home naming, SessionEnd hooks, managed config paths and update behavior, and auto-review reviewer persistence.

The non-adjacent Windows filesystem commits are grouped because openai/codex#33632 removes the GeneratedDefault variants and special handling introduced by openai/codex#33430, leaving the target already aligned with the net design.

The non-adjacent agent-settings stack groups the configuration foundation, activation of configured defaults, and the resulting post-role validation fix; the interleaved agent_type schema change remains separate because it conflicts with Every Code's role and provider-routing UX.

The Every Code prealignment tree was consulted for product-sensitive collaboration, session-hook, image-generation, MCP, and context behavior; classifications retain those boundaries rather than treating upstream Codex internals as authoritative UX.
Only the WorldState and audio sequences are grouped because their later commits require the earlier behavior; direct-parent adjacency alone was not used as a stacking rule.
The only multi-commit stack is core-c-extension-compaction because the second patch consumes the StepContext API introduced by the first; no other adjacent commits are genuine dependent stacks.

The upstream SHAs exist in the comparison worktree object database via openai/main, but git cherry reports all 16 as not present on the target HEAD, so classifications are behavioral rather than ancestry-based.

Several upstream patches touch files/modules absent from the target branch, so adapt means port the behavior while preserving Every Code product behavior, especially external-agent spawning, session provenance, fork compatibility, and rollout/session storage compatibility.

Deferred executor-capability, route-aware HTTP, external-memory, and shadow-selection work depends on upstream foundations outside this bucket; no dependency between the multi-commit stacks in this result is asserted.

Adaptations should preserve Every Code's stronger skill trigger/delegation guidance, plugin precedence and migration UX, agent authority boundaries, originator/branding values, and compatibility aliases.
The two multi-commit stacks intentionally span non-adjacent input indices because they modify the same implementation path; independent interleaved commits remain singleton rows.
implementationStatus values of missing or partially_implemented identify work still absent from the compared Every Code worktree.
Model, provider, auth, guardian, and user-facing instruction changes are marked adapt where upstream behavior must preserve Every Code-specific routing, security policy, terminology, or branding.

Every Code release and ownership boundaries are preserved: upstream openai/codex repository names, releases.openai.com, R2 bucket/prefix, workflow topology, and branding are not treated as directly transferable.

The R2 commits are grouped only because they evolve the same upstream publisher implementation; the alternate-source installer remains a separate future adaptation without a dependency on the rejected R2 stack, and the two non-code commits are independent not-applicable cleanups.

riskFlags.reason: Model-visible skill catalog entries can exceed 1,000 tokens and the current core budget lacks the upstream hard cap; implementation requires manual context-contract review and a per-item cap below 10,000 tokens.
Hook additional context is model-visible; limits above 1,000 tokens require manual review and zero must not disable the hard bound.
The current bad-image retry path rewrites model-visible history; adopt the upstream no-rewrite behavior before adjacent history work.
Realtime delegation text is currently injected through a manual XML wrapper; move it under ContextualUserFragment independently of tail provenance.
Cwd changes can leave AGENTS.md instructions stale; preserve bounded instruction diffs and existing context ordering when adapting the refresh.

rows.rationale: The target still rejects ThreadHistoryMode::Paginated in thread/start, has no resume backwards cursors or thread/searchOccurrences method, and cannot materialize the upstream legacy views. Lower-level paginated storage primitives already exist, so the missing work is a coherent app-server enablement stack rather than a product-policy decision.

The target already has mailbox-delivery phases and queue-only follow-up coverage, but defer_mailbox_delivery_to_next_turn treats any buffered item as same-turn work, inject_if_running does not re-enable current-turn mailbox delivery, and task completion does not wake trigger mail after clearing the active turn. Port the boundary semantics into the target's reordered completion path without bypassing Every Code's background auto-review scheduling.

The target still scans roots sequentially in core-skills and lacks the upstream root-loader snapshot types. Port the bounded shared semaphore and ordered merge into Every Code's existing host/plugin root model rather than transplanting the upstream module layout.

Patch adds a pre-render block to AppEvent::CodexOp and a render_before_submit path gated on CodexOpTarget::AppEvent; worktree event_dispatch.rs has plain CodexOp handling and input_submission.rs displays unconditionally with no CodexOpTarget marker present in tui/src.

Every Code already converts external-agent commands into skills, but plugin manifests have no commands path and plugin installation does not create generated skills. Reuse the existing conversion semantics while preserving Every Code naming, generated-cache placement, native-skill precedence, and nonfatal install behavior.

This patch only restructures tests and snapshots under core/src/context/world_state. The target has no such module and tests its bounded ContextualUserFragment implementation through different files, so creating the upstream test harness would add no runtime coverage or product-currentness value.

The target has a Claude-oriented import pipeline but none of the stack's connector-candidate response, migrationSource/Cursor adapter, MEMORY item, stable session sub-error taxonomy, or providerId attribution. Port the capabilities onto the target's newer service layout while preserving Every Code's CODE_HOME/.code paths and product copy; the prealignment product tree has no newer source-picker flow to retain verbatim.

The target has the same sequential list_directory_connectors then list_workspace_connectors flow. The upstream concurrency preserves ordering, filtering, error tolerance, and compatibility, so it can be adopted directly with its regression coverage.

The target does not contain ext/mcp or the SelectedExecutorPluginMcpContributor path this optimizes. Revisit only after Every Code chooses or ports the selected-capability extension architecture; the concurrency itself is compatible once that prerequisite exists.

Sending source=codex would falsely attribute Every Code traffic and violates the product-branding boundary. If the endpoint later supports a neutral or Every Code-specific attribution value, that should be handled as a separate product integration rather than importing this Codex-only wrapper.

Every Code already watches skill roots, clears caches, and supplies host skills per turn, so runtime changes can become visible. It lacks the upstream world-state delta projection and unchanged-fragment suppression; adapt that behavior to Every Code's incremental context contract and stronger skill instructions without replacing its provider UX.

The target lacks the selected-capability-root model, session/mcp_runtime.rs, ext/mcp, and the MCP contributor context that consumes ready environment roots; its capability-root references are Windows sandbox concepts instead. Defer this dependent pair until Every Code adopts the deferred-environment and selected-capability authority model, then retain validation, runtime refresh, root limits, first-location precedence, and conflict warnings.

The second patch removes the GeneratedDefaultPath and GeneratedDefaultSpecial variants, their conversions, and the special Windows filtering introduced by the first. The target never carries those variants and already detects protected metadata that requires direct runtime enforcement while using the legacy projection for existing metadata, so applying the intermediate representation would create dead API churn and no net upstream alignment.

The upstream patches add HistoryPosition/history_base and subagent_history_start_ordinal, inherit paginated history for spawned/forked subagents, and resume paginated agents from model context. The target worktree has earlier paginated history_mode support, but no HistoryPosition/history_base/subagent_history_start_ordinal fields and the spawn path has Every Code-specific external-agent, provenance, shell snapshot, and fork-gate behavior. This should be adapted, not cherry-picked directly.

The target's approval scenario runner still verifies the result and returns without shutdown_and_wait. The upstream change is a focused test-lifecycle cleanup that preserves the original verification Result, reduces leaked background work, and does not alter Every Code runtime or approval UX.

The target's windows_sandbox_uses_elevated_backend returns true for proxy_enforced or an explicitly elevated level, its command-exec path starts configured proxies on Windows, and the old compatibility validators removed upstream are absent. The same user-visible behavior is already present through the target's divergent Windows sandbox implementation.

Upstream removes the loader as unused, but the target deliberately exports it and merged dedicated managed-policy parse-failure recovery plus regression coverage immediately before this classification baseline. Deleting network_proxy_loader.rs would undo owned Every Code config/runtime behavior and a maintained public surface even though the workspace has no direct caller.

The target TokenUsage and analytics paths expose cache-read data but no cache-write field; port the accounting through Every Code's provider-neutral usage model without changing model selection, provider routing, or branding.

The target already has codex-external-agent-migration, but substantial detection and service orchestration remain in app-server and session handling is split into an Every Code-specific crate. Continue the ownership cleanup in reviewable stages while preserving protocol conversion at the app-server boundary and Every Code's source-specific migration behavior.

Upstream changes the paginated thread-history projection to track final_answer phases for summary items. The target preserves message phases in app-server protocol projection, but LocalThreadStore does not implement the upstream paginated list_turns/list_items module and the legacy turns-list summary still selects the last agent message regardless of phase. The behavior is desirable but must be mapped onto Every Code's current projection/reconstruction layout.

The target retains custom generate/edit action guidance and a no-postamble image UX. Add only the longer initial/wait yield guidance where Every Code's code-mode directive supports it, retaining generatedImage(result) and the existing Every Code interaction contract.

The target heuristic only recognizes direct rm -f or rm -rf plus a simple sudo recursion and plain shell-command extraction. It misses combined, split, long-form, post-operand, env-wrapped, nested-shell, pipeline, control-flow, substitution, and trap forms, and lacks the safer forced-rm rejection reason. The upstream safety behavior is compatible with Every Code's approval model and should be adopted with its policy and integration coverage.

The target's MCP tool-call items and lifecycle events do not define template_id/templateId, and the remaining template IDs belong to plugin catalog summaries rather than tool-call metadata. The upstream cleanup therefore has no local surface to modify.

No cache_write_input_tokens or cacheWriteInputTokens field exists anywhere in the target protocol, schema, app-server tests, or core usage types. Adopt after the companion protocol token-accounting commit is available.

The target protocol already defines FunctionCallOutputContentItem::EncryptedContent, but CallToolResult conversion only recognizes ordinary text and images and returns structured_content before examining encrypted MCP content. Add the metadata-aware conversion and precedence rule so encrypted payloads are not serialized as plaintext or discarded, retaining the existing wall-time wrapping and MCP output UX.

The target already has agents.max_threads, roles, job limits, interruption behavior, explicit model/reasoning validation, and separate V2 fanout settings, but lacks agents.enabled, the canonical max_concurrent_threads_per_session alias, persisted resolved defaults, configured native-subagent defaults, full-fork override support, and post-role validation. Adapt the stack without replacing Every Code's built-in and installed external agent catalog, provider-routing policy, metadata-hiding controls, broader reasoning catalog, or parent-model inheritance when defaults are unset.

Upstream exposes agent_type only when user-configured agent_roles is nonempty. Every Code always merges built-in roles and enabled external agent models into the spawn description, uses agent_type and task metadata for provider routing, and already has hide_spawn_agent_metadata for intentional concealment. Applying the upstream predicate would hide valid choices and degrade capability self-reporting; the removed support_agent_type field is already absent locally.

Every Code has explicit selection and command-triggered implicit invocation but no upstream dynamic-selector or shadow-experiment framework. Defer the algorithm suite until Every Code defines evaluation, telemetry, and activation rules that cannot bypass mandatory/delegated skill semantics or its own orchestration policy.

The target has no wait_for_environment tool, StepContext, starting-environment state, or context/world_state module. Adding the text alone would advertise an unavailable blocking tool. Revisit this pair with the deferred-environment UX and implement the guidance as a bounded ContextualUserFragment that preserves Every Code's model-visible context limits and avoids duplicate retained instructions.
Every Code actively uses codex-realtime-webrtc from the TUI and app-server realtime flows, so applying this deletion would remove a live product capability rather than clean up dead code.

The target apps processor still uses only last_notified_apps and emits whenever the merged list changes; it lacks the sent_app_list_update and cached-page gating added upstream. This is a contained correctness fix with no Every Code UX conflict.

The target releases the process-store lock before terminal interaction, but the write_stdin handler is not parallel-enabled and UnifiedExecProcess has no per-session interaction lock or prune guard. Port those controls onto the target's extended network-approval, terminal-event, interrupt, and code-mode paths so independent terminals overlap without racing reads, writes, exit cleanup, or active-session eviction.

The target has no app/read request, AppsRead protocol types, connector metadata cache, or enriched connector fields. The second commit directly extends the first endpoint and should land after it as one ordered stack.

The target persists and restores agent-role identity metadata, but ensure_v2_agent_loaded resumes the cold subagent from the caller's current config without applying the stored role's model, provider, reasoning, instructions, or backend settings. Adapt the reload fix through Every Code's role resolver and provider-routing/external-agent layer while restoring the runtime approval reviewer, cwd, shell policy, and permission profile after role application.

The target's immutable TurnContext already keeps environment selections stable during a turn and resolves updates for the next turn, satisfying the first commit's core invariant. However, its model-visible-layout test explicitly records that cwd changes do not refresh AGENTS.md, and it lacks upstream StepContext/world_state modules. Port only the readiness and bounded instruction-diff behavior through the target's existing ContextualUserFragment/context manager so Every Code prompt ordering and context caps remain intact.

The comparison tree's codex-rs/code-mode/src/runtime/value.rs still accepts http(s) and data image URLs. The upstream hardening is relevant, but it must be adapted to Every Code's older integrated code-mode implementation rather than copied from the newer split protocol/runtime layout.

The target resolves a session originator and default clients carry the process value, but standalone extension requests do not receive a non-default thread-specific value. Port the propagation and validation while recognizing Every Code originators and retaining compatibility aliases instead of adopting a Codex-only trusted-name list.

The frozen patch only changes the freeform apply_patch description and its exact test expectation. The target still uses the older imperative string in core/src/tools/handlers/apply_patch_spec.rs; its grammar and higher-level Every Code patch instructions remain separate, so this is a low-risk wording sync.

The target external-agent migration API does not yet expose memory items or the external_agent_import resource workspace this fixes. Preserve these scope, frontmatter, managed-project-marker, and no-synthetic-rollout requirements when memory migration is introduced, but do not add an isolated downstream fragment now.

Worktree bottom_pane/approval_overlay.rs still declares ApprovalRequest::Exec { thread_id, .. } etc. inline and brace-destructures the variants (pre-refactor shape); the field set matches upstream so only the structural wrapping is absent.

The upstream patch only avoids taking a writer slot in repair_legacy_recency_migration_version. The target worktree has no such repair function and instead has Every Code migration tests for a remapped visible-thread-index migration floor. There is no direct production behavior to port unless a future migration import recreates the upstream repair hook.

Reject this stack for the reserved amazon-bedrock provider. Every Code keeps that provider canonical and AWS-authenticated, permits only aws.profile and aws.region overrides, and directs custom endpoints, command auth, and headers through a separately named custom provider. The managed Bedrock account schema and logout assertion follow-up are not applicable without importing the rejected transport and account model.

grep for canAcceptDirectInput/can_accept_direct_input/parent_owned/view_only in tui/src finds no capability plumbing (only unrelated 'view only' text); the change touches protocol common.rs / v2 thread_data plus app-server processors and broad TUI composer/session flows, a large cross-cutting feature tied to V2 ownership semantics.
The exact target test remains present with timeout_ms set to 5000. Adopting the upstream 20000 value is a direct flake-hardening change and does not alter production behavior.

The target has no app/installed method, AppsInstalled protocol types, installed connector runtime projection, or forceRefresh path. The endpoint exposes existing runtime truth and can be adopted without changing Every Code's user-facing app UX.

Patch edits chatwidget/reset_credits.rs and usage.rs and adds UsageLimitReset app events; none exist in the worktree and grep for redeem/UsageLimitReset returns nothing. Every Code's chatwidget/rate_limits.rs implements a different lower-cost-model switch prompt instead — an account/usage flow Every Code intentionally owns.

This is bounded, optional telemetry around data Every Code already serializes and does not change web-search behavior. Adopt it using the existing telemetry compatibility namespace unless Every Code has established a replacement metric namespace.

The target lacks capabilityRoots/discoverV1, selected-capability roots, ext/mcp, and the upstream discovery cache. Defer until those authority models are reconciled with Every Code orchestration; then port the bounded batch/snapshot design without retaining the upstream opt-in feature flag.

The target still builds model-visible realtime delegation XML through a manual wrapper, so the ContextualUserFragment extraction is applicable now. The transcript_tail_flush source marker remains dormant until the missing tail producer and V3 handoff substrate are staged; adapt the contract-safe fragment independently and defer only the provenance marker.

The target realtime start surface supports the earlier V1/V2 path and has no V3/Frameless substrate, CodexResponseHandoffMode, BEM routing, or initialItems. This stack also depends on deferred realtime tail-provenance work. Stage the substrate and Every Code-owned contextual handoff path first, then reassess the user-facing routing portion as an adaptation.

The target test_codex() still has no default feature mutator, while its shell snapshot suite explicitly enables Feature::ShellSnapshot where needed. It also already supports ThreadStoreConfig::InMemory in thread_manager, but approvals.rs does not select it, so the test-isolation behavior is absent without affecting runtime shell or rollout behavior.

The target supports TurnEnvironmentSelection and exec-server environments but has no multi_exec_server_sandbox suite module or equivalent two-server isolation coverage. Port the regression against the target's current environment-selection API; it validates existing security behavior and introduces no product policy.

The patch specifically changes MultiAgentMode::Custom and multi_agent_mode_hint_text, neither of which exists in the target. Every Code's collaboration-mode fragment already filters empty developer instructions, and the prealignment product tree follows the same collaboration-mode behavior, so importing the upstream mode-specific message state would add unused parallel UX.

This is test-only cleanup across upstream's feature registry, exec defaults, and Linux sleep inhibitor constant. Every Code's feature registry and coverage have diverged, and deleting locally useful checks produces no runtime or product-currentness benefit.

The target still defines dispatch_any as an allow(dead_code) wrapper and only its tests call it; production routing already calls dispatch_any_with_terminal_outcome. The upstream cleanup therefore maps directly to an internal API simplification and matches the target's positional-literal comment convention.

codex-rs/code-mode/src/service.rs directly constructs requested millisecond sleeps for initial execution and Poll. Its cell-control state machine differs from upstream's SessionRuntime, so the 10-second threshold and one-second grace need a focused port with nested-tool timing coverage.

Target role_tests.rs and unified_exec/mod_tests.rs contain the same ignored tests that upstream removes, including the obsolete timeout-cap and completed-session assertions. This is maintenance-only cleanup and does not remove active Every Code role, exec, or sandbox coverage.

Worktree wrapping.rs still defines and calls word_wrap_lines_borrowed, and footer.rs still declares the #[allow(dead_code)] PairProgramming/Execute variants with their label/style arms; both deletions remove only unused/filtered-out code. Verify Every Code has no plan to re-enable pair/execute footer chips.

These patches are a real sequence: collaboration state first, then realtime state, then permissions plus stable fragment hashing. The target has no context/world_state module or Session::build_world_state_for_step and still injects these fragments directly from context_manager/updates.rs and session/mod.rs. Every Code's prealignment tree instead has product-owned context_ledger/context_timeline work, so a direct backport could alter persisted context, resume, and agent configuration behavior; stage it only with the missing foundation reconciled.

Worktree app_server_session.rs constructs ExternalAgentConfigImportParams { migration_items } only, with no source or migration_source fields, so the upstream field the patch edits does not exist in Every Code's protocol shape.

Upstream publishes replaceable connection sets through McpRuntime and moves resource clients off a session manager handle. The target has no codex-mcp resource_client.rs and keeps a session-owned Arc<RwLock<McpConnectionManager)> whose resource operations serialize under the manager guard. This precursor has no independent Every Code user-visible benefit and should be staged with the later adapted MCP binding/catalog work instead of adding intermediate runtime plumbing.

The target rollout list path already has bounded head/tail summary logic and read_session_meta_line support, but codex-rs/cli/src/doctor/thread_inventory.rs still calls RolloutRecorder::load_rollout_items to derive thread IDs. The upstream doctor header-reader should be adapted to avoid scanning whole large rollouts.

The target lacks the upstream HookEventName::SessionEnd and teardown runner. The Every Code prealignment tree already has a separate ProjectHookEvent::SessionEnd contract, so the upstream bounded archive/delete/unload behavior should be integrated with that product hook model rather than added as a second independently firing session-end mechanism.

The target PluginSummary and remote plugin cache paths have no mustShowInstallationInterstitial value. Preserving the nullable remote policy is compatible with Every Code and lets clients fail closed when policy is unknown.

Worktree app/history_ui.rs still hardcodes the Codex.exe path and uses 'Codex Desktop'/'Codex App' text (history_ui.rs, tooltips.rs, slash_command.rs); the CLI desktop_app/mac.rs+windows.rs bundle discovery is the functional core. Preserve Every Code desktop-handoff branding while adopting the launch-script/bundle-discovery logic.
Every Code has the same append-only history concept but keeps its own codex-lab path and TUI search behavior; port the bounded scanner while preserving local record schema, cursors, and branding.

Worktree bottom_pane/chat_composer_history/ has no search_batch module (glob returns no files) and lacks the batched app_event/thread_routing plumbing, confirming the feature is unimplemented; it has no account/branding surface, adapting only to Every Code's chat_composer_history layout.

The target already has local managed network-proxy infrastructure but no RemoteNetworkProxyLaunchConfig path through its exec-server boundary; add the remote capability without weakening Every Code's network approval and provider policies.
The target update-target enums and mapping only accept UNLISTED and PRIVATE. Adding LISTED is a direct protocol/backend compatibility update with focused integration coverage.

Worktree agent_navigation.rs defines AgentPickerThreadEntry with only nickname/role/is_closed; grep finds no stopped_threads/mark_running/mark_stopped/SubAgentActivityKind/path_backed anywhere in tui/src, and open_agent_picker derives status dots solely from is_closed. Both commits edit fields/paths that are absent, and neither lands without the other.

The target supports realtime audio transport but has no generic UserInput::Audio/LocalAudio or FunctionCallOutputContentItem::InputAudio variants. The second commit builds directly on the first protocol primitive; upstream deliberately omits unsupported audio from TUI/model paths, so adoption does not force a new Every Code audio UX.

No inline_visualization.rs in worktree; grep for codex-inline-vis/inline_visualization finds only terminal_visualization_instructions.rs (an unrelated ASCII-visual instruction string), and the commit's markdown/streaming/controller edits target an architecture Every Code has diverged from.

The target's codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/command_runner.rs still unconditionally calls command.arg(&handler.command), matching the faulty upstream shape. The cfg(windows) raw_arg handling is narrowly scoped and preserves Every Code behavior on non-Windows platforms.

The upstream search change targets codex-rs/thread-store/src/local/thread_history/search.rs and UserInput audio variants; the target has neither that module nor Audio/LocalAudio user-input variants. The defs.bzl unit_test_args addition is also absent. This can be carried forward when importing newer paginated search/audio or Bazel test target changes.

The commits are dependent: #33932 forwards audio, #33982 keeps unsupported models from receiving it, and #34385 preserves it across history, truncation, tool outputs, and thread projection. The target has realtime microphone transport but UserInput only supports text and images, with no InputAudio variant or audio preparation. The companion app-server protocol stack supplies the shared primitives; upstream deliberately keeps TUI audio attachment display optional, so adoption need not change Every Code's current realtime voice UX.

The target has base_sqlite_options/open_sqlite in codex-rs/state/src/runtime.rs with WAL, Normal synchronous mode, busy_timeout, shared migration/telemetry handling, and path-based filename configuration. Upstream extracted this to state/src/sqlite.rs and tightened test path assumptions. Equivalent runtime behavior exists; importing upstream would be a file-layout adaptation.

Worktree cwd_prompt.rs/session_lifecycle.rs already implement the prompt and remote short-circuit, but grep for resume_cwd/ResumeCwd in config/src/types.rs returns nothing, so the persisted preference is absent while the surrounding infrastructure exists.

The target catalog already contains Every Code-specific model variants, personality text, and branding but intentionally differs on context windows and visibility; review metadata field by field instead of copying upstream values wholesale.

The target already retries sampling and emits the same human-readable warning, and its RemoteCompactionV2 branch already has structured fields. Only the Sampling branch lacks turn_id, retries, max_retries, and sampling_error plus the focused logging regression test, so the retry behavior exists but its diagnostic context is incomplete.

Every Code already compresses rollouts in thread storage but its doctor inventory still uses plain-path assumptions and Codex-specific naming; adapt the parity scan to the existing codex-lab storage layout.

Glob of tui/src/streaming shows chunking/commit_tick/controller/mod/table_holdback but no render.rs, and markdown_render/ has no streaming.rs; the commit's new modules and controller rewrite do not map onto Every Code's files.

Worktree reasoning_shortcuts.rs matches the pre-patch line the commit replaces and AppEvent::UpdateReasoningEffort(Option<ReasoningEffort>) is defined; verify Every Code's handler applies the effort without persisting to match intent.

Worktree status_controls.rs set_status/set_status_header return no value, chatwidget/streaming.rs uses active_stream_tail helpers absent upstream, and frame_requester.rs has no test_channel — a different approach to the same goal.

Worktree thread_to_transcript_cells takes &Thread in a different module than upstream's thread_transcript.rs, confirming the by-value refactor is absent and requires adaptation to Every Code's layout.

Worktree markdown_stream.rs is at the pre-patch state (finalize_and_drain_source, commit_complete_source returns String, committed_source_len) and streaming/controller.rs carries Every Code divergence, so the refactor applies but needs adaptation.

Worktree app/side.rs calls plain app_server.fork_thread with no fork_side_thread/ForkPresentation/exclude_turns, and session_lifecycle.rs still uses the unconditional liveness-refresh gate with no side_threads short-circuit; #34199 fixes races introduced by #34198 so they are order-dependent, and porting depends on whether app-server ThreadForkParams exposes exclude_turns.
Worktree insert_history.rs still takes lines: Vec<HyperlinkLine> and tui.rs passes batch.lines.clone(), confirming the allocation is present and the change is a clean adopt.
Worktree history_cell/mcp.rs still defines CompletedMcpToolCallWithImageOutput holding _image: DynamicImage, and the placeholder output does not depend on retaining the image.

Worktree markdown_render.rs still has the per-char next_column_to_shrink and &self compute_column_widths, and wrapping.rs/terminal_hyperlinks.rs remap helpers are pre-patch, so the optimization is absent and touches three files.
The entire change is about inline_visualization_context in streaming/render.rs; Every Code has no InlineVisualizationContext/DIRECTIVE_PREFIX and no streaming/render.rs module.
Worktree exec_cell/model.rs still has formatted_output, with_added_call, and completion checks on c.output.is_none(), confirming the duration-based completion marker is absent.
Worktree app/thread_events.rs has no push_notification_ref/Cow-based push_notification_inner, so it is pre-patch; the variant skip-list must be reconciled with Every Code's protocol.
Worktree has no markdown_render_cache.rs and AgentMarkdownCell lacks the rendered_lines cache; the visualization bypass in the upstream cache has no counterpart in Every Code.
Worktree diff_render.rs still has the owned struct Row { path: PathBuf, change: FileChange } with change: change.clone(), confirming the borrow-based refactor is absent.

The comparison tree's codex-rs/exec/src/lib.rs invokes maybe_backfill_turn_completed_items before should_process_notification. Moving it into the existing active-thread/turn filter is a local correctness fix for Every Code's multi-agent exec event stream.

The target already persists thread names through title/rollout-name indexing, stores Git info, and has memory_mode support and memory filters. It lacks upstream's dedicated threads.name column and paginated-specific resume protection that avoids reapplying stale initial Git metadata. The stack should be adapted to Every Code's schema and rollout/session compatibility rules.
